### Key Points
- **Overview**: Champions of the Future is an international karting series founded in 2020 by the RGMMC Group, aimed at developing young drivers through high-level competitions aligned with FIA standards. It serves as a preparatory platform for global events like the FIA Karting World Championship.
- **Structure and Expansion**: It includes the Euro Series, Academy Program, and recent expansions to America and the UAE. Classes typically cover Mini, OK-Junior (OKJ), and OK, with emphasis on fairness through equipment lotteries.
- **Notable Aspects**: Partnerships with F1 Academy promote female participation, offering subsidies and pathways to higher motorsport levels. Research suggests it has helped launch careers, though success varies as in any junior series.
- **Controversies and Challenges**: While praised for accessibility, some debates exist around cost controls and geographic focus, with evidence leaning toward positive impacts on diversity but room for broader inclusion.

### What is Champions of the Future?
Champions of the Future is a karting championship series that focuses on nurturing young talent in motorsport. Launched in 2020, it organizes events across Europe and beyond, using standardized rules to ensure fair competition. Drivers compete in categories like OK and OK-Junior, often as a stepping stone to professional racing.

### Main Series and Events
The flagship Euro Series runs multiple rounds each year at tracks like Portimao in Portugal and Kristianstad in Sweden. The Academy Program, started in 2023, offers an "arrive and drive" format where equipment is provided, making it easier for newcomers. Recent announcements include a North American series starting in 2026, in partnership with K1 Speed.

### Partnerships and Impact
It collaborates with F1 Academy to support female drivers, providing discounts and branded gear. This has helped identify talents who progress to formulas like F4. While not all participants reach the top, the series is seen as a valuable entry point, with alumni competing in higher categories.

For more details, see sources like the official website (https://www.championskarting.com/) and announcements from partners (https://www.f1academy.com/).

Champions of the Future (COTF) is an international karting series organized by the RGMMC Group, a promoter specializing in motorsport events. Established in 2020, it provides competitive platforms for young drivers aged 8 and older, aligning with Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA) regulations to prepare participants for higher levels of racing, such as the FIA Karting World Championship. The series emphasizes fairness through measures like equipment lotteries and cost controls, and it has expanded to include regional programs in Europe, the Middle East, and North America. Notable for its partnerships, including with F1 Academy to promote gender diversity, COTF has produced drivers who have advanced to single-seater formulas. As of 2025, it hosts multiple series with over 200 entrants per event in categories like OK, OK-Junior, and Mini.

## History
The series was launched in 2020 by the RGMMC Group, a company founded by James Geidel that had previously organized events under the Rotax Max Challenge banner. The inaugural Euro Series aimed to fill a gap in international karting by offering high-quality competitions with FIA-homologated equipment, focusing on OK and OK-Junior classes. Early events were held amid the COVID-19 pandemic, with rounds in locations such as Adria in Italy and Wackersdorf in Germany.

In 2022, COTF introduced a Winter Series to provide off-season racing opportunities, featuring tracks like Franciacorta in Italy. The Academy Program debuted in 2023 at Al Forsan International Sports Resort in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, as an arrive-and-drive initiative to reduce barriers for aspiring drivers. This program expanded in 2024 with F1 Academy support, emphasizing female participation through subsidies and talent scouting.

By 2025, the series had grown to include a UAE regional championship and announced a North American expansion in partnership with K1 Speed, set to begin in 2026. The Euro Series that year featured five rounds, culminating in titles for Kenzo Craigie in OK and Lewis Baglin in OK-Junior. The Academy Program concluded its second season with champions in multiple categories, including Markas Silkunas in OK-N Senior.

COTF has adapted to industry trends, incorporating esports elements like the KartSim × RGMMC Esports Cup in 2025. It also launched related initiatives, such as the F4 Racing Academy in September 2025, offering seats in Formula 4 for top performers.

## Series and Events
COTF organizes several championships, each with distinct formats and locations to maximize driver development.

### Euro Series
The core competition, held annually since 2020, consists of four to five rounds across European circuits. Events include free practice, qualifying, heats, and finals over weekends. In 2025, rounds were at Portimao (Portugal), Zuera (Spain), Kristianstad (Sweden), Franciacorta (Italy), and a fifth venue. The series uses FIA CIK classes, with tires and fuel supplied uniformly.

### Academy Program
Introduced in 2023, this arrive-and-drive series targets drivers aged 8–15, providing chassis, engines, and suits to control costs. It features six double-header weekends, with categories including Mini 60 (ages 8–11), OK-N Junior (ages 11–14), and OK-N Senior (ages 14+). Equipment is allocated via lottery for fairness, with suppliers like Parolin/TM for Mini and Kart Republic/IAME for others. The 2025 season included events in the UAE, Spain, Italy, and elsewhere, with live broadcasts on Motorsport TV.

### Other Series
- **UAE Series**: Launched in 2025 at Al Forsan and other tracks, it mirrors the Academy format for regional talent.
- **America Series**: Announced on December 2, 2025, in partnership with K1 Speed, it aims to bridge U.S. indoor karting to professional levels, starting in 2026 with unspecified classes.
- **Shifters and Winter Series**: Supplementary events for KZ shifter karts and off-season racing, such as the 2025 Shifters round in Valencia, Spain.

Events emphasize driver education, including physical training and media workshops. The series has hosted over 140 drivers per round, with grids filling quickly.

## Classes
COTF adheres to FIA karting regulations, with classes divided by age and engine type:

- **Mini 60**: For drivers aged 8–11, using 60cc engines; includes sub-categories like U10.
- **OK-N Junior (OKJ)**: Ages 11–14, with restricted 125cc engines.
- **OK-N Senior (OK)**: Ages 14+, with unrestricted 125cc engines.
- **Shifters (KZ/KZ2)**: Gearbox karts for older or master drivers.

All classes use homologated chassis and engines, redistributed daily to prevent advantages.

## Notable Drivers
Several COTF participants have progressed to higher motorsport levels. Alumni include:

- Luna Fluxá, 2024 Academy OK-N Senior champion, who advanced to Spanish F4 with Campos Racing in 2026.
- Julia Montlaur, 2024 Academy winner in another class, joining the Mercedes-AMG Junior Programme.
- Kenzo Craigie, 2025 Euro Series OK champion and 2024 FIA OK-Junior World Champion.
- Markas Šilkūnas, 2025 Academy OK-N Senior champion.
- Niccolo Perico and Wynn Godschalk, 2025 Academy Mini champions, with Godschalk topping the U10 sub-category.

Other drivers like Oliver Bearman and Rafael Câmara, now in Ferrari's Driver Academy, competed in early COTF events before winning world titles elsewhere. Female drivers such as Atiqa Mir have set records, including the highest female qualifying in Mini class history.

## Partnerships
COTF collaborates with organizations to enhance accessibility:

- **F1 Academy**: Since 2024, it supports up to nine female drivers per category with 30% entry discounts, branded karts, and testing opportunities. The partnership expanded in 2025 to include 27 drivers for 2026, focusing on talent identification.
- **K1 Speed**: For the American series, providing infrastructure and pathways from indoor to outdoor karting.
- **Minerva’s Virtual Academy**: Offers online education for young racers.
- **Scouting Advisors**: Includes Gwen Lagrue from Mercedes-AMG for spotting potential.

These alliances aim to address barriers like costs and gender imbalance, though some sources note ongoing challenges in global diversity.

## Champions
The following tables list overall champions for major series. Results are based on final standings after heats and finals.

### Euro Series Champions
| Year | OK Champion | OK-Junior Champion | Source |
|------|-------------|--------------------|--------|
| 2020 | Not fully contested due to pandemic; inaugural winners included drivers in preparatory events | N/A | |
| 2021 | Various round winners; overall titles not centralized in early years | N/A | |
| 2022 | Round-specific; e.g., Portimao and Zuera heats won by emerging talents | N/A | |
| 2023 | Competitive season with multiple heat winners | N/A | |
| 2024 | Titles awarded; specific names include Nathan (OKJ-related) | N/A | |
| 2025 | Kenzo Craigie | Lewis Baglin | |

### Academy Program Champions
| Year | Mini Champion | OK-N Junior Champion | OK-N Senior Champion | Source |
|------|---------------|----------------------|----------------------|--------|
| 2024 | N/A | Clancy (leader mid-season) | Luna Fluxá | |
| 2025 | Niccolo Perico (Mini); Wynn Godschalk (U10) | Clancy | Markas Šilkūnas | |

Shifter category champions in 2024 included Anthony Abbasse in KZ2 Masters.

champions of the future
-----------------------

Launched in 2020 by promoter RGMMC, the Champions of the Future series has become a must for the best international drivers and teams. Some of the biggest names in the world have already won the competition, some of them now in single-seaters. In 2024, the Champions of the Future Euro Series will be held over five meetings optimally spread between March and September. Based on the FIA Karting regulations, this season promises to be rich in quality and quantity in the OK and OK-Junior categories.

[![Image 14: KZ: Hiltbrand and Van Walstijn the heroes of the day The event got off to a perfect start for Danilo Albanese (KR Motorsport) with pole position, but the Italian then had to let other drivers take centre stage... Giuseppe Palomba (Maranello Kart), Mattéo Spirgel (CPB Sport) and Senna Van Walstijn (CPB Sport) shared the three heats, before Van Walstijn went on to win the Super Heat ahead of Pedro Hiltbrand (Birelart Racing). In the intermediate classification, Palomba took the lead before the Final, but was immediately overtaken by Hiltbrand after a few corners. A magnificent duel then began between Hiltbrand, Palomba and Van Walstijn, with David Trefilov lying in wait (Formula K SRP Factory Team). As the laps went by, Senna Van Walstijn proved to be the fastest, confirming this with the best lap of the race. He overtook Palomba and then Hiltbrand to cross the finish line 1st after 24 laps. However, he was given a five-second penalty, leaving the victory to Hiltbrand. Behind them, Trefilov collided with Palomba while trying to secure his place on the podium and was also penalised. Lorenzo Travisanutto (Parolin Motorsport), who had won his duel with Daniel Vasile (CL Racing Team) and then defended against Albanese's comeback, had the satisfaction of taking 3rd place. Jean Nomblot (CPB Sport) and Viktor Gustafsson (CRG Racing Team), who finished 6th and 7th respectively, also showed strong potential at Franciacorta. The list of retirements grew as the laps went by, including names such as Renaudin, Spirgel, Lorandi, Camplese, Pex, Ippolito and Denner. Although he did not win this Final, Van Walstijn consoled himself with the 2025 Champions of the Future Shifters title ahead of France's Jean Nomblot and Italy's Giuseppe Palomba, who saved 3rd place by a few points ahead of Spirgel and Hiltbrand. [![Image 15: KZ2: Maxim Orlov reigns supreme The winner in Valencia, Maxim Orlov (CPB Sport) has been impressive since securing pole position in Qualifying. He had to retire from one heat due to a collision at the start, but regained the advantage over Markus Kajak (Formula K SRP Factory Team) and Timo Jüngling (CPB Sport) thanks to his success in the Super Heat. In the Final, Orlov got off to a perfect start. Kajak looked dangerous in the early laps, before having to let his opponent pull away to victory. A technical problem eventually forced Kajak to retire and Orlov took the chequered flag as the winner with the fastest lap of the race and a lead of almost five seconds. There was plenty of action in the pack. Kimi Tani (LA Motorsport) took 2nd place on the podium ahead of a strong Simon Rechenmacher (Dörr Motorsport), who had already won one of the two Super Heats. A five-second penalty dropped Jayden Thien (CPB Sport) from 4th to 8th place. Having climbed up from 11th and 14th place respectively, the two British drivers Jüngling and Noah Wolfe (VAR by Birel) finished 4th and 5th ahead of one of the revelations of the weekend, Hungary's Menyhert Krozser (CRG Racing Team). Already crowned FIA Karting European Champion, Orlov logically won the series with a comfortable lead over Germany's Max Schleimer and the Netherlands' Kasper Schormans, who finished just one point ahead of his compatriot Jayden Thien. Final series standings: 1 Max Orlov 2 Max Schleimer (GER) 3 Kasper Schormans (NED) 4 Jayden Thien (NED) 5 Kimi Tani (FIN) …](https://i2.ytimg.com/vi/5EkpO6lLhA0/hqdefault.jpg) KZ2 Event Highlights | Shifters Round 2 - Franciacorta | 2025 Champions of the Future](https://www.championskarting.com/wp-content/plugins/feeds-for-youtube/img/lightbox-placeholder.png)

[![Image 16: KZ2 Masters: Angelo Lombardo makes the difference Former KZ2 European Champion Angelo Lombardo (Maranello Kart) set a very fast pace in this competition for drivers aged 35 and over. Pole position, victories in the three heats, then in the Super Heat and in the Final, Lombardo logically climbed onto the top step of the podium. Anthony Abbasse (CPB Sport) kept the suspense going by getting off to a better start than the Italian. But after a few laps, the Italian resumed his triumphant march. The group behind Lombardo created the suspense. As determined as ever, Davide Fore (IPK Factory Team) successively overtook Riccardo Nalon (Erre Esse Motorsport), Daniel Bray (Modena Racing Team) and then Abbasse to settle permanently in 2nd place. Manuel Cozzaglio then picked up speed to catch up with Abbasse. He tried his luck to earn a place on the podium, but the two drivers collided three laps from the finish. After setting the fastest lap of the race, Nalon regained 3rd place and held off Bray, who was very close behind, until the end. Kristijan Habulin (TB Kart Racing Team) drove at a high pace to move up to 5th place ahead of Alessio La Martina (KR Motorsport), who had been the star of the weekend. ### [Fierce battles in Shifters at Franciacorta](https://www.championskarting.com/fierce-battles-in-shifters-at-franciacorta/)

Minerva’s Virtual Academy offers bespoke education for racers aged 12 – 18. Unlike traditional schools, the Academy can be accessed anywhere in the world, at any time, and offers a world-class, flexible education fit for the 21st century. Pupils no longer have to miss school to attend training, track events, or race weekends.

The online school, which has won many awards since its launch, is run by Lawrence Tubb, a former head of department at Wycombe Abbey (one of the UK’s most prestigious private schools), and blends smart, interactive self-study (supported by the pupil’s personal mentor) with live online classes that can be managed around the athletes’ schedule. Young racers in particular are assisted by a unique mentoring programme that helps to develop them professionally as well as academically, overseeing their mental wellbeing whilst teaching soft skills such as public-speaking, self-confidence, and self-discipline.

Its pupils, who are able to choose from over 20 subjects at GCSE or A Level, are welcomed into a thriving, global community of talented pupils in sport and the arts, including Olympic hopefuls, West End performers, musicians, actors, and social media influencers, setting them up with brilliant friendships and connections for later on in life.

For the most bespoke solution (very popular in karting), private tutors from the school provide 1-2-1 teaching either in person or online, to ensure the pupil receives maximum attention and support on their path to success.

Champions of the Future America Announced

![Image 4: The 10-race schedule for Champions of the Future America.](https://www.k1speed.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/COF-Header.jpg)

WINCHESTER, Calif., December 2, 2025 — RGMMC Group, a global leader in international karting promotion and the organization behind the highly acclaimed “Champions of the Future” series, today announced a landmark partnership with K1 to launch **Champions of the Future America**, a new initiative designed to elevate the next generation of American motorsport talent and create new pathways through the sport.

This collaboration marks a major milestone in bringing a new format of competitive karting platform to the U.S. market, giving young American drivers access to the same professional standards, organization, technology, and competitive environment that have helped shape numerous current elite motorsport athletes.

“**America is the largest karting market**, and partnering with K1 allows us to bring a proven development pathway to a country with passion, scale, and talent. While bridging the gap between Europe and the United States,” said James Geidel, CEO of RGMMC.

K1, a recognized leader in American karting and motorsport entertainment since 2003 with brands K1 Speed and K1 Circuit, will bring its national footprint, industry knowledge, and strong community of young racers to the partnership. Together, RGMMC and K1 will introduce a series of events and programs focused on doing things differently.

**“K1’s ambition is to introduce casual indoor go-kart racers to the world of outdoor karting as part of the pathway to professional motorsport,**” said K1’s Founder and CEO, David Danglard. “By partnering with Champions of the Future in North America, we can achieve this goal and give our drivers the best opportunity to pursue their racing dreams.”

Race Series Features
--------------------

*   A professionally organized race series aligned with international standards
*   Pathways for U.S. drivers to access global karting competitions
*   State-of-the-art event management and technological support

### 2026 Schedule

Rd 1 January 31- February 1**K1 Circuit**

Rd 2 February 28 -March 1**K1 Circuit**

Rd 3 March 21- 22**K1 Circuit**

Rd 4 April 18-19 **K1 Circuit**

Rd 5 & 6 May 29-31**Spring Mountain Double header 3 Day Event**

Rd 7 June 27-28**K1 Circuit**

Rd 8 July 18-19**K1 Circuit**

Rd 9 August 29-30**K1 Circuit**

Rd 10 September 26-27 **K1 Circuit**

Categories to be included: Mini, IAME X30, KA100, and KZ classes.

A new global championship aiming to increase female participation and inclusion in national and international karting championships, by breaking down the barriers to entry. To do this, the series will include cost control measures, such as a limit on entry fees and a chassis lottery, to decrease the financial requirements for competitors.

F1 Academy will support three female drivers in each category, who will receive a financial subsidy to help fund their drive, along with F1 Academy-branded kart and race suit for each of the nine drivers.

**HOW DOES THE CHAMPIONSHIP WORK?**

The series will be comprised of three mixed gender categories, Minis (ages 8-11), Juniors (ages 11-14) and Seniors (ages 14+), will compete in six double-header race weekends, with at least one race taking place outside of Europe.

Additionally, the three top female drivers in the Seniors category will also be invited to an official F1 Academy test at the end of the 2024 season helping develop a pathway for karting talent to progress to F1 Academy.

![Image 6: default image](https://res.cloudinary.com/prod-f2f3/ar_16:9,c_fill,dpr_1.0,f_auto,g_auto,h_675,w_1200/v1/FA/Global/guide_to/269A3477)

**WHAT ARE ITS GOALS?**

Talent identification will be a key focus to help create a pipeline of identified talent amongst young girls aged 8-15, with the goal of entering F1 Academy.

Working closely together with Susie Wolff, Champions of the Future President James Geidel will look to identify up and coming talent within karting and look to capture promising drivers who show the skills and traits needed to progress through the junior levels.

**HOW TO GET INVOLVED**

If you’d like to find out more or get involved with the Championship, please visit the [Champions of the Future Academy website](https://www.championskartingacademy.com/).

Champions of the Future Academy Program
---------------------------------------

**Powered by RGMMC**

The _Champions of the Future Academy Program_ is a premier **Arrive and Drive** international karting series designed to develop the next generation of motorsport talent. Created by RGMMC and aligned with FIA sporting standards, the program combines elite competition with comprehensive driver education—offering young racers the experience and global exposure needed to launch professional careers while **controlling costs.**

Featuring three competitive categories—**Mini 60**, **OK-N Junior**, and **OK-N Senior**—the Academy brings together rising stars from around the world to compete in world-class events across the globe. Including on-track racing, physical training, workshops, and media day, making it a complete development platform for future champions.

Whether you’re an aspiring driver or sponsor, the Champions of the Future Academy is where the next generation begins.

![Image 25: Susie Wolff wears a white collared shirt with the F1 Academy logo](https://www.championskartingacademy.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/SWTransparent1.png)

Discover Your Drive 

 “With so much momentum building around F1 Academy, we must continue to strengthen the pipeline of talent coming into our sport. We look forward to this collaboration with Champions of The Future which will create a clear pathway from karting into F1 Academy. COTFA will operate a lottery system for the chassis and engines plus implement a fixed budget, giving us the opportunity to identify the top talent across all age groups. We will also provide the best in the senior category with an F1 Academy test, giving them a chance to prove themselves to our teams. Champions of the Future shares F1 Academy’s vision to increase female participation, create opportunity and allow clear progression up the motorsport ladder.”

Susie Wolff

Managing Director of F1 Academy

### [why race cotfa?](https://www.championskartingacademy.com/)

The **Champions of the Future Academy Program** is designed to offer young drivers a world-class racing experience with a strong focus on development, exposure, and affordability. Here’s why it stands out:

### ![Image 32: 🏁](https://s.w.org/images/core/emoji/17.0.2/svg/1f3c1.svg)**Elite Competition**

Compete against top young talents from across the globe in a highly professional and competitive environment, using CIK-FIA homologated material.

### ![Image 33: 🌍](https://s.w.org/images/core/emoji/17.0.2/svg/1f30d.svg)**International Exposure**

Race at renowned circuits and gain visibility in front of sponsors, and talent scouts from higher motorsport categories.

### ![Image 34: 💸](https://s.w.org/images/core/emoji/17.0.2/svg/1f4b8.svg)**Cost-Controlled & Affordable**

The Academy Program is structured with **strict cost controls** to ensure fair competition and **keep participation costs relatively low** compared to other international karting series. This makes it an ideal choice for families and teams looking for maximum value without compromising on quality.

### ![Image 35: 📈](https://s.w.org/images/core/emoji/17.0.2/svg/1f4c8.svg)**Career Development**

The program serves as a proven pathway to higher levels of motorsport, including OK/OKJ, FIA Karting, and even Formula 4. Many successful drivers have been on this journey.

### ![Image 36: 🧠](https://s.w.org/images/core/emoji/17.0.2/svg/1f9e0.svg)**Education & Growth**

Drivers receive not only race experience but also lessons from Formula medicine and media professionalism—all vital for a successful career.

### ![Image 37: 🔧](https://s.w.org/images/core/emoji/17.0.2/svg/1f527.svg)**Top-Level Equipment**

Access to competitive, well-maintained karts, engines, and technical support, ensuring a level playing field for all participants.

### ![Image 38: 🤝](https://s.w.org/images/core/emoji/17.0.2/svg/1f91d.svg)**Networking & Support**

Build lasting connections with teams, coaches, and industry professionals who can support your progress through the motorsport ranks.

### [whats the weekend format?](https://www.championskartingacademy.com/)

*   Thursday collection of material
*   Friday free practice all day
*   Saturday – Free practice, time qualifying, 2 heats and a Final
*   Sunday – Free practice, time qualifying, 2 heats and a Final

### [F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVE SELECTION PROCESS](https://www.championskartingacademy.com/)

*   We are looking for talented drivers with experience in karting to represent F1 Academy Discover Your Drive at the Champions of the Future Academy Program 2025.

*   3 drivers in each class will be selected to represent F1 Academy Discover Your Drive and receive a 30% discount on entry fees.

*   To be eligible for the selection process you must sign up before the 22nd of December to the 2025 Champions of the Future Academy Program.

*   If you don’t get selected for 2025 you can still compete in the Champions of the Future Academy Program, improve your skills and try again at the end of 2025.

### [What is the material used](https://www.championskartingacademy.com/)

The Champions of the Future Academy Program elected chassis and engine suppliers will be Parolin powered by TM Kart Engines for the Mini class, and Kart Republic powered by IAME for the Junior and Senior classes.

### [How do we ensure fair play](https://www.championskartingacademy.com/)

Ensuring equal material and fairness is the highest priority of the series. After each day all the engines are returned to the manufacturer to be checked and re-distributed via a lottery.

The manufacturers are onsite to provide technical support and help you with any quesitons you may have.

### [Whats included in the package?](https://www.championskartingacademy.com/)

Those drivers signed up for the year receive a race suit, kart, awning space, trolley and work bench, tires and fuel.

The driver must provide their own mechanic and tools. Onsite we have tools such as drills and flat benches.

20.description: In this episode of K1Speed, we take a journey through the history of go-karting, tracing its development from a grassroots hobby to a global phenomenon. From the hot rod scene in Southern California to the modern-day competitions, we'll explore the key players, innovations, and trends that made go-karting what it is today. Whether you're a seasoned enthusiast or a newcomer to the world of go-karting, this video is a must-watch for anyone interested in the story behind the sport.

13.title: Champions of the Future 2025 - Spanish and Canadian anthems ring out under the Campillos sun
13.description: 01 April 2025 - Over the years, the Champions of the Future Euro Series has established itself as an essential series at the highest level of international karting. Launched in 2020, it has seen many of the top drivers who currently shine in the most important single-seater championships, including Formula 1 in the case of Andrea Kimi Antonelli. The series organised by RGMMC
13.content:
Published: 01 April 2025

Columns: Races

Over the years, the Champions of the Future Euro Series has established itself as an essential series at the highest level of international karting. Launched in 2020, it has seen many of the top drivers who currently shine in the most important single-seater championships, including Formula 1 in the case of Andrea Kimi Antonelli. The series organised by RGMMC lives up to its name by showcasing young hopefuls every year, who can also prepare for FIA Karting events in the best possible conditions. The opening of the 2025 season celebrated the victories of two great talents: Spaniard Christian Costoya in OK and Canadian Ilie Tristan Crisan in OK-Junior.

**A benchmark organisation, many drivers and exciting races**

The first of the five events in the Champions of the Future Euro Series got off to a great start in southern Spain, with almost 190 drivers taking part: 96 in OK and 91 in OK-Junior. The success of the series continues, with its high standards of organisation. In addition to the presence of quality circuits on its calendar, RGMMC is constantly improving its race control technology with the installation of some forty cameras around the track to ensure greater sporting fairness, not forgetting perfect live streaming of the races. New functionalities have also been introduced, allowing viewers to benefit from a maximum amount of data: information on tyres, comparisons between drivers, detailed race presentations, interviews, practical information, etc. The result is an even improved television production, in partnership with Motorsport.tv for the broadcast.Three and a half years after the last Champions of the Future Euro Series event at Campillos, the 1,580-metre circuit located in Andalusia to the north of Malaga provided the ideal playing field for the drivers to show off their skills, while the teams were able to work in excellent conditions thanks to the very pleasant weather that accompanied the participants from 26th to 29th March 2025. Tyre manufacturer Maxxis supplied the participants' tyres with its usual professionalism, while RGMMC stepped up the training of its team over the winter to ensure smoother organisation and interaction.

**OK: Costoya imperious in his home country**

Spaniard Christian Costoya (Parolin Motorsport) immediately gave his rivals a warning of his ambitions, with an almost perfect weekend: pole position, four wins out of five in the heats, 1st place in the Super Heat and a controlled Final with a lead of more than two seconds over those chasing after him. Only Sweden's Viktor Gustafsson (CRG Racing Team) managed to beat him in a heat! Other drivers to cross the finish line as winners during the event: Iacopo Martinese (Cetilar Racing), the Czech Jindrich Pesl (Tony Kart Racing Team), the Greek Stylianos Taxiarchis Kolovos (KR Motorsport), the Italian Filipo Sala (Forza Racing) and the British Joe Turney (KR Motorsport), Roman Kamyab (RFM) and Aston Sharp (CL Racing Team) in the heats, as well as the Belgian Dries Van Langendonck (Prema Racing) in a Super Heat, revealing a very open competition.Over the course of the Final (19 laps), Costoya won after two superb overtakes on the drivers who had overtaken him on the first lap: Turney and then Van Langendonck. Having started 5th, Kenzo Craigie (Prema Racing) made a brilliant comeback to take 2nd place, while Martinese won his duel with Van Langendonck to complete the podium. 5th-placed Turney showed that he will be a force to be reckoned with in 2025. The Briton finished ahead of the two Australians Lewis Francis (KR Motorsport) and James Anagnostiadis (Prema Racing). Spaniard Eloi Martinez (Birelart Racing) improved from 27th to 8th place. Belgian Thibaut Ramaekers (VDK Racing) and Canadian Jensen Burnett (Forza Racing) rounded off the top 10 with the fastest lap going to Frenchman Louis Cochet (VictoryLane Racing).

**OK-Junior: Crisan's rise to prominence**

After the pole position achieved by Australian William Calleja (Forza Racing), many drivers showed themselves capable of aiming for the podium. Six different drivers shared the heats and Super Heats: Calleja, of course, but also Turkey's Iskender Zulfikari (Forza Racing), Canada's Ilie Tristian Crisan (Tony Kart Racing Team), Dean Hoogendoorn (Prema Racing), Bosco Arias (RFM) and Henry Domain (Forza Racing).The first lap of the Final was very lively, with Crisan immediately moving up from 3rd to 1st place. A slow procedure was initiated at the start of the race following a collision between several karts in the middle of the field, which fortunately was not serious. At the restart, Crisan flew to victory with the fastest lap in his pocket, while a breathless duel involved several drivers. Hoogendoorn managed to make the difference to take 2nd place on the podium ahead of Calleja, despite Domain's ambitions, who was in 2nd place during the Final.The Walz brothers (KR Motorsport) put in a strong showing for the United States, with Drew in 5th place and Devin in 8th. Britons Will Green (KR Motorsport) and Noah Baglin (Prema Racing) managed to squeeze in between them. The latter made a brilliant comeback, having had to make do with 46th place in Qualifying on Friday. Italian Bruno Blanco (Parolin Motorsport) was in the top five after the start, but dropped back to 10th behind Frenchman Luka Scelles (VictoryLane Karting).

Press Release by: RGMMC - 01/04/25

18.title: RGMMC launched Champions of the Future
18.description: RGMMC launched Champions of the future a Cik classed based series.
18.content:
Published: 30 September 2019

Columns: News and Previews

Champions of the Future is a new series by RGMMC based on CIK categories.

2020 will be a very busy year for the European karting drivers and teams, RGMMC launched a new international series called Champions of the Future.

It’s a 3 races-based championship that will include all the international classes, OKJ, OK and KZ2 plus the 60 Mini (thing as result of the new category homologation).

The championship will start in Wackersdorf (GER), from 12 to 15 March, then will continue in Zuera from 2 to 5 April and it will end in Kristianstad from 25 to 28 June.

RGMMC President James Geidel has explained us the reason behind this new series.

**What’s aim of the series? To offer a sort of first taste of international races?**

_«The idea is to give the market another chance to get into the cik classes and try out ok. As at the moment if you want to try ok you have to join directly the FIA races DKM or WSK. Which apart from the FIA it’s all based in Germany and Italy. A lot of teams want to try the ok but need another platform to do so»._

**Is the presence of the Mini linked to a possible future implementation of the mini itself in the FIA Karting champs? (A sort of “test”) or the things are completely separed?**

_«As we do the IAME Euro Series we notice that the mini is really growing and we think we should also promote the class how it’s homologated by CIK from next year and open that market also for those stakeholders»._

**How did RGMMC decided the locations? Are them linked to 2020 FIA Karting calendar?**

_«The calendar is based on 3 rounds because the calendars are already really full so makes no sense todo a 6 round series. With 3 it’s also easy for teams thinking to try ok to commit to 3 rounds. Of course Germany and Sweden are already well established with Cik classes and we have good relationship with those countries. Plus Italy already have so many events doesn’t make sense to go for the first year. As for Spain we already work with the Spanish federation and it’s a good way to demonstrate the class»._

### Karting Champions League now welcoming 2026 Winter Series Entries

### Numerous International Teams registered for the 24 Hours Karting of Italy

Just a few days after entries opened in early December, a strong number of teams have already registered for the 24 Hours Karting of Italy, promoted by CRG and scheduled for March 14–15 at the Castelletto di Branduzzo circuit (Italy). Several countries are already represented, with teams coming from China, the Czech Republic, Spain, Romania, France and Belgium, just to name the first registered entries. The 2026 edition is shaping up to have a clearly international profile in both admitted categories: PRO, dedicated to more experienced teams, and SILVER, designed for more amateur crews with all drivers over 18 years of age.

### 2025 Prokart Challenge Championship podium finishers honored

The 21st season of the ProKart Challenge concluded this past October, completing the five events with six rounds of competition for the Superkarts! USA regional program. Eleven different class champions were crowned following the action at the K1 Circuit finale event.

### ROK Cup Italia 2026 – calendar change

The 2025 ROK season came to the end with the Rok Festival, which took place on November 29 and 30 at the Franciacorta Karting Track, and now all attention is on the 2026 ROK calendar.

### 24 Hours Spa Karting: twice rather than once in 2026!

The 24 Hours Spa Karting is returning! Although the 2025 edition could not take place, organiser One Day Karting has decided to make up for it in 2026 with two events: one with a Sodikart fleet on 13 and 14 June, followed by a second with the traditional Biz Le Mans Twins on 5 and 6 September. Each with their own unique characteristics, these two events complement each other and both promise to be exciting and international.

### Australian Hamish Campbell finishes seventh at FIA Arrive & Drive World Cup

### The 24 Hours Karting of Italy 2026 will take place on March 15 in Castelletto (Italy)

### New beginnings in Abu Dhabi as the UAE Series launches in style

The Champions of the Future Academy Program UAE Series made its debut at the Al Forsan International Sports Resort in Abu Dhabi, opening a new chapter for RGMMC’s global arrive-and-drive platform.

### Superkarts! USA confirms location for 2026 Winter Series

Since its inception in 2018, the Superkarts! USA Winter Series has been situated in the state of Florida, hosting events at Ocala Gran Prix, AMR Homestead-Miami Motorplex Presented by MG Tires and, most recently, the Orlando Kart Center. Each venue has provided its own uniqueness and history throughout the eight years of the program. Year nine of the SKUSA Winter Series will present a new location, with both events of the 2026 schedule to be held at the Speedsportz Racing Park in New Caney, Texas.

### ROK Cup Italia 2026 - Previews and calendar

With the 2025 ROK season coming to an end, all eyes are already on 2026, a year that promises to be exciting thanks to new developments and unmissable events!

### Birelart: Korus Group is Born

The Group brings together eight leading Italian companies in an integrated motorsport ecosystem: the first capable of bridging the worlds of karting and racing cars.

Karting Australia is pleased to confirm the dates for the 2026 Australian Kart Championship, setting the stage for another exciting season of top-level competition across the nation.

### A major sporting and organizational success for the 2025 Rental Kart World Contest

New format, same outstanding success for one of the most prestigious events in CRG’s Rental calendar: the Rental Kart World Contest. The 2025 edition of this renowned international meeting, raced with CRG Centurion karts, took place at the 7 Laghi Kart Track in Castelletto di Branduzzo, Italy, from October 17th to 19th. For this 6th edition, the race format brought back a mix of Sprint Cup and Endurance Cup, as it was in the inaugural 2016 event. Castelletto hosted the Sprint titles on Saturday — with over 100 drivers competing across Junior, Silver, and Pro categories — and the Endurance Cup on Sunday, a 6-hour race featuring 34 teams on the grid.

### Final Winners of 2025 Decided at ProKart Challenge

The 2025 season concluded for the ProKart Challenge following the action on October 11-12 at the K1 Circuit. The Winchester, California, facility welcomed the Superkarts! USA regional program to close out its 21st season. A total of 161 entries battled around the 1.1-mile ‘Pro Track’ course for the sixth and final round of the 2025 championship.

FIA Karting Circuit Allocation: A Question of Diversity
=======================================================

* * *

[![Image 58: A 21x15 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.kartcom.com/wp-content/themes/kartcom/assets/images/flags/FR.svg)](https://www.kartcom.com/news/2025/10/18/lattribution-des-circuits-fia-karting-une-diversite-en-question/)

[Circuit](https://www.kartcom.com/en/news/category/circuit-en/)[Federation](https://www.kartcom.com/en/news/category/federation-2/)[International](https://www.kartcom.com/en/news/category/international-en/)[Reflection](https://www.kartcom.com/en/news/category/reflection/)[FIA](https://www.kartcom.com/en/news/tag/fia-en/)

The [2026 FIA Karting season](https://www.kartcom.com/en/calendar/?category=&competition=&organiser=53818&place=&country=) will be no exception: once again, Italy will host the lion’s share of international events. This is no trivial matter-it raises a genuine question about the geography of international karting, its underlying logic, its strengths… and its limits.

![Image 60: FIA Karting Events by Country (2021-2026) pie chart shows the data for Italy (11), Spain (7), Sweden (5), France (4), Germany (4), Belgium (3), Portugal (3), Denmark (2), Bahrain (1), Czechia (1), Slovakia (1), and the United Kingdom (1)](https://www.kartcom.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/kartcom_website_ksp_fia_karting_events_by_country_20212026.webp)

Over the past six seasons (2021 to 2026), Italy has hosted 11 FIA Karting events, far ahead of Spain (7), Sweden (5), or France (4). The peninsula alone accounts for nearly a third of the calendar. Franciacorta, Cremona, Sarno, Viterbo, La Conca… the list grows almost every year, while other countries, sometimes equally deserving, appear only occasionally-or disappear entirely from the map.

**A Sport That’s “International”… With a Strong Italian Flavor**

 It’s hard to deny Italy’s influence in karting history. The country is home to most factories, the industry is powerful, the circuits highly professional, and the organizational experience well proven. It’s also difficult to overlook that almost 90% of the world’s chassis, engines, or accessories are made in Italy.

 But does that mean the horizon should stop there? Drivers themselves, coming from all over the world, would undoubtedly welcome more variety in tracks and cultures. Spanish, Nordic, German, French, or British circuits-all now meet FIA standards for safety, infrastructure, and media coverage. Le Mans, Genk, Kristianstad, Zuera… all have proven they can successfully host a World or European Championship.

**A Question That Goes Beyond the Official Calendar**

 The debate is not new, and it goes far beyond the FIA itself. Private series, such as the WSK, focus almost exclusively on Italian tracks, leading to a concentration of events at the same venues, at the expense of other outstanding circuits. Champions of the Future-designed as a preparatory championship for FIA events-generally follows the federation’s official calendar, which means the same geographical choices are repeated year after year.

 So why not consider a better balance? Isn’t karting, by nature, the most international gateway to motorsport?

 Some circuits tick every box but still struggle to find their place in the official program. The most striking example is Alahärmä in Finland, last visited for a memorable World Championship in 2019, and still widely regarded as a benchmark in terms of facilities. Of course, this is not an exhaustive list; several other high-level international circuits have also been left out of the FIA calendar in recent years.

**Balance: A Way Forward?**

 This geographical concentration also raises questions about the development of karting in other regions-regions rich in talent and passion. Giving new circuits a chance is an investment in the sport’s future, a way to stimulate innovation, and an invitation for everyone to take part.

 In 2026, Bahrain will make its return to the international stage-a sign that broader horizons are possible. But for now, this remains the exception: the general trend is still very much European… and above all, Italian.

**The Numbers Speak for Themselves-But the Debate Remains Open**

 Should we continue to prioritize the comfort of the familiar, or dare to take a more adventurous path? Karting remains the number one training ground and springboard for the sport’s future stars, but wouldn’t it benefit from genuinely broader diversity in its international destinations?

Summary Table: FIA Karting Events by Country and Circuits (2021–2026)*

 1 – Italy – 11 – Franciacorta (3), Cremona (3), Sarno (4), Viterbo (2), Val Vibrata (1), Adria (1), La Conca (1)

 2 – Spain – 7 – Valencia (4), Zuera (3), Campillos (2), Aragón (1)

 3 – Sweden – 5 – Kristianstad (5)

 4 – France – 4 – Le Mans (2), Val d’Argenton (1), Aunay-les-Bois (1)

 4 – Germany – 4 – Wackersdorf (3), Mülsen (2)

 6 – Belgium – 3 – Genk (3)

 6 – Portugal – 3 – Portimao (3)

 8 – Denmark – 2 – Rodby (2)

 9 – Slovakia – 1 – Slovakia Ring (1)

 9 – Czechia – 1 – Trinec (1)

 9 – UK – 1 – PF International (1)

 12 – Bahrain – 1 – Bahrain International Karting Circuit (1)

_*Except for any errors or omissions on our part._

**In brief**

 – Italy’s dominance has only grown, with 11 events over six seasons.

 – France returns to the spotlight in 2026 with the World Championship back at Le Mans.

 – Northern Europe (Sweden, Germany, Belgium, Denmark) remains steady.

 – In November 2026, Bahrain will again host a FIA Karting event-the first outside Europe since the last edition held there in 2016.

**Conclusion: The Weight of Politics in the Calendar**

 In the end, it’s likely that the sport’s governing bodies prefer to avoid unnecessary risks. Every year, the first proposals come from the ASNs (National Sporting Authorities), who select and submit their candidate circuits; the FIA then finalizes the venues and dates, which are ratified by the World Motor Sport Council. Nothing shocking-this is an eminently political process, with each side defending its own interests and traditions, all under the banner of safety, logistics, and organizational guarantees.

 But we mustn’t forget that, in motorsport, politics is not always synonymous with development or fairness. This search for stability can sometimes stifle innovation, or slow down the emergence of new playing fields for drivers and teams. Opening up the calendar to more international circuits does not mean ignoring the historical expertise of some regions; it’s simply about giving karting the chance to remain a universal, dynamic sport, true to its founding spirit: diversity, discovery, and openness.

Ultimately, the question remains: should we always choose the safety of the status quo, or take a bold step to build a truly international future?

 Everyone will have their own answer. But the issue goes far beyond a mere line on a calendar.

26.title: Why We Sell Sodi – Championship‑Winning Kart Chassis & Driver Development | Nashville Karting Group
26.description: Discover why we chose Sodi. As a Tennessee dealer, we trust Sodi for its world championship wins, elite driver development, and race‑proven performance and support.
26.content:
![Image 1: black and white bed linen](https://assets.zyrosite.com/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,w=1920,fit=crop/AQEyOb90gbh57oe3/jon-YbNJgWLEXLsP7g3V.JPG)

Why we chose Sodi chassis – official Tennessee dealer
-----------------------------------------------------

As an official Tennessee dealer for Sodi chassis, we chose to align with the world’s largest kart manufacturer for one simple reason: performance backed by results. On this page, we’ll share why we believe in Sodi, what sets their chassis apart, and how they’ve helped shape champions around the world.

### Our Journey to Sodi

My karting journey started in Southern California, driving a CRG chassis. Like many racers, I tried different brands early on, but it wasn’t until a friend let me drive his Sodi that everything clicked. The balance, responsiveness, and build quality stood out instantly. Just two weeks later, I made the switch. That same friend later moved to France and raced Sodi professionally—proof that I wasn’t imagining the difference.

Years later, after more experience and deeper involvement in the sport, I had the opportunity to bring Sodi to other racers by becoming an authorized dealer. It felt like the right fit—not just because of the results on track, but because of the culture behind the brand.

January 8, 2012

January 20, 2012

December 22, 2011

![Image 2: black and white bed linen](https://assets.zyrosite.com/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,w=1920,fit=crop/AQEyOb90gbh57oe3/jon-YbNJgWLEXLsP7g3V.JPG)

### Why Sodi?

**Global leader** – Sodikart is the world’s largest kart manufacturer, producing both competition and rental karts at its French factory and exporting to over 100 countries.

**Financially sound** – Sodikart generates approximately **€80 million in annual revenue**, with about **70% of sales coming from international exports**, reinforcing its position as a dominant player in the global karting market.

**Innovation & quality** – Sodi invests heavily in research and development, holding multiple patents and adhering to strict quality standards. Their focus on performance and reliability makes them the trusted choice for both professional teams and rental fleets worldwide.

**Customer support** – From the Sodi Racing Team to their global dealer network, the company prioritizes service and driver support—something we've experienced firsthand as an authorized dealer.

### Championships & Podiums (2024–2025)

Sodi’s results in recent seasons underscore its technical excellence:

*   **2024 FIA Karting World Championship (KZ)** – **Giuseppe Palomba** (Sodi/CPB Sport) became world champion while team‑mate **Senna Van Walstijn** finished second.

*   **2024 European Championship (KZ2)** – **Mattéo Spirgel** took the title, and **Van Walstijn** was runner‑up in KZ.

*   **WSK Final Cup 2024** – Sodi drivers **Maksim Orlov** and **Kasper Schormans** claimed victory, with five Sodi machines in the top ten.

*   **Champions of the Future Shifter 2024** – **Anthony Abbasse** dominated the KZ2 Masters (pole and all heats), and **Van Walstijn** climbed from the back to finish second in the KZ final.

*   **2025 WSK Super Master Series** – The new **Sigma 2025 chassis** immediately reached the podium with **Mattéo Spirgel**; **Senna Van Walstijn** grabbed pole, and **Maksim Orlov** set the fastest lap.

*   **2025 FIA European Championship** – Sodi’s dominance continued: **Spirgel** won the KZ European title, and **Maksim Orlov** swept all three rounds to become **KZ2 European champion** with a full Sodi podium.

These results demonstrate that Sodi chassis perform at the highest level and in varied conditions. When you race Sodi, you’re using equipment capable of winning world and European championships.

![Image 3: black and white bed linen](https://assets.zyrosite.com/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,w=1920,fit=crop/AQEyOb90gbh57oe3/jon-YbNJgWLEXLsP7g3V.JPG)

### Sodi Alumni in Formula 1

Many top‑level drivers began their careers on Sodi karts. Three of the most notable are **Pierre Gasly,****Charles Leclerc, and Esteban Ocon**:

*   **Pierre Gasly** joined the **Sodi Racing Team in 2009** and immediately won the **French KF3 Championship**. The following year, he finished **second in the European Championship** and stood on the podium at the Monaco Kart Cup. A Formula 1 feature notes that he finished second in the **2010 European Karting Championship** with Sodi equipment.

*   **Charles Leclerc** raced Sodi karts from 2008, winning the **French Cadet Championship** and the **Bridgestone Cup,** and later the **Monaco Kart Cup** and **Bercy Masters**.

*   **Esteban Ocon** also benefited from Sodi’s support; a Sodi Racing USA release credits Sodi promoter Thierry Germanovitch with guiding the karting careers of **Leclerc, Gasly, and Ocon**.

Their success stories underscore how Sodi equipment can be a stepping stone from grassroots karting to Formula 1.

### Driver Development & Events

Sodikart believes in making karting accessible. Through its **3MK Events** division, the company organises France’s **National Series Karting**, the **Challenge Rotax France**, and the international **Sodi World Series (SWS)**. These “arrive and drive” programmes allow newcomers to race identically‑prepared karts without owning equipment, making them ideal for driver development. Many participants progress from SWS races to national and international competitions.

![Image 4: black and white bed linen](https://assets.zyrosite.com/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,w=1920,fit=crop/AQEyOb90gbh57oe3/jon-YbNJgWLEXLsP7g3V.JPG)

### Join the Sodi Family

Our decision to represent Sodi was driven by both personal experience and objective results. From the moment I first drove my friend’s Sodi, I was hooked. The chassis responded intuitively, gave me confidence and, most importantly, made racing fun. The fact that Sodi dominates world championships and has launched the careers of Gasly, Leclerc, and Ocon only reinforces our belief.

We remain respectful of other brands—after all, I began on a CRG chassis and learned a lot from it. However, we feel Sodi offers the best balance of performance, quality, and support for our customers. Whether you’re an aspiring racer looking for your first championship or a hobbyist seeking the pure joy of karting, **Sodi provides a platform that can take you as far as you want to go**.

**Interested in trying a Sodi chassis?** Get in touch and let us help you join a community of passionate racers who trust in Sodi’s innovation and championship pedigree.

### Have Questions? Get in Touch

Need more details on engine rebuilds, maintenance, or karting resources? Contact **Nashville Karting Group** for expert advice and support. We're here to help!

30.title: Discover Julia Montlaur, Mercedes AMG Junior Programme's latest addition
30.content:
**_French karting talent Julia Montlaur has been announced as the latest addition to the Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Junior Programme for 2025, joining fellow female racers Luna Fluxa and Doriane Pin, forming a female 25% of the driver roster._**

![Image 1: Madeline Stewart, JDX Racing, Porsche Carrera Cup North America](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/aed0c4_7425434af60a464baf26fd14f913b1d2~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_740,h_463,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/aed0c4_7425434af60a464baf26fd14f913b1d2~mv2.jpg)

Photo credits: Mercedes Benz AG

French karting talent Julia Montlaur has been announced as the latest addition to the Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Junior Programme for 2025.

Born in La Seyne-sur-Mer, France, the 12-year-old began her motorsport journey at an incredibly young age, first riding motocross at just two and a half years old. By the time she was eight, she discovered karting and quickly decided to pursue racing on four wheels.

Montlaur entered her first competitive karting race in 2021 and has steadily climbed the ranks ever since. Over the past two seasons, she has primarily focused on national competitions in France, consistently delivering strong performances.

A key moment in her development came when she participated in a two-day Iron Dames selection event, where she had the opportunity to experience a professional racing environment. This experience further fueled her ambition, and she went on to reach the finals for the French Championship in both 2023 and 2024 in the Mini class.

In 2024, she also finished ninth in the IAME Series France championship, establishing herself as one of the country’s most promising young drivers. Montlaur now embarks on her first season as a Mercedes junior driver and is set to make the step up to the OK Junior category.

She will compete in the Champions of the Future Academy Program as well as the FFSA Academy in France, aiming to continue her rapid development within the highly competitive international karting scene.

Montlaur joins an increasingly diverse Mercedes junior roster, which now features 25% female representation, alongside Luna Fluxa Cross and Doriane Pin. She will be looking to follow in the footsteps of Fluxa, who joined the programme in 2022 at the age of 11 and went on to win the Champions of the Future Academy title in 2024 with an outstanding season in the Senior category.

She also draws inspiration from fellow Mercedes academy graduates, including George Russell and Kimi Antonelli—who will race for the F1 team this season—citing the Italian as one of her racing heroes.

The Ultimate karting championship past and current drivers who have advanced to excel at all levels of motorsport.

Born in Epsom, UK, in 2010, Kenzo is the latest driver to join the Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team’s Junior Programme. Success in the Cadet karting class has seen Kenzo ascend to the top ranks of the British karting scene.

His breakthrough year came in 2021 as he earned a ticket to the Rotax Max Grand Finals in Bahrain. In 2022, Kenzo dominated the Cadet class, winning the Ultimate Karting Championship Series, British Kartmasters (GP Plate), British Karting Championship (O Plate), and finishing as the British Karting Championship Vice-Champion.

In 2023, Keno made the step up to the Junior class, competing in UK and International Rotax under the Mercedes AMG umbrella.

Rising star Gabe Fairbrother will take the first steps into car racing for the 2023 season after agreeing a move into the Quaife MINI CHALLENGE Trophy with the EXCELR8 squad.

The highly-talented teenage racer will join the Suffolk-based squad on the back of a successful career in karting, where he firmly established himself as a driver to watch with several impressive performances on track.

Having already secured multiple race wins in the early stages of his career, the 2022 season saw Fairbrother secure the Junior Rotax class of the Ultimate Karting Championship, following in the footsteps of drivers such as Mercedes F1 Junior – and British F4 race winner – Daniel Guinchard.

Fairbrother’s decision to move into the Cooper class of the MINI CHALLENGE for his first taste of car racing comes as part of a longer-term vision to forge a career in GT competition in the coming years, and will see him look to benefit from the motorsport ladder put in place by the EXCELR8 team to aid young drivers embarking on the early stages of their career.

2021 saw Noah make history as the first cadet racer to win the double at KartMasters Grand Prix in IAME cadet and Honda cadet.

He also became the British Open Champion, PF Plate Champion, this was on top of securing 3rd in the IAME British Championship and becoming Vice-Champion in the Honda British Championship as well as securing many podiums and pole positions in the LGM Championship. Following this success, Noah also finished in the top 10 at the IAME World finals in Italy.

With lots learned, 2022 was a big year, Noah's first in big karts and competing in two major national championships in MiniMax, becoming the 2022 Ultimate karting champion !

Noah now races in OKJ competing all over Europe with the likes of 2020 Ultimate karting champion Nathan Tye.

![Image 9: ALUMNI TEXT nw-02.png](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/b636c8_1d1da1656caf4696a650142f897409eb~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_600,h_45,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/ALUMNI%20TEXT%20nw-02.png)

![Image 10: The image showcases a go-kart and a race car navigating separate curved sections of a race track, with the go-kart on the left and the race car on the right, each demonstrating speed and precision](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/b636c8_347eaba47a80443ba9a7e5b195654f3c~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_1301,h_609,al_c,q_90,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/b636c8_347eaba47a80443ba9a7e5b195654f3c~mv2.png)

Daniel was born in the United Kingdom in 2006 and was signed to the Mercedes F1 Team’s junior programme ahead of the 2022 season.

Since 2016, he has been working his way up the karting ladder and started competing at a national level in 2018, where he was vice British champion in the Honda Cadet class.

2021 was a breakthrough season for Daniel, winning the the Ultimate Karting Championship in Rotax Junior. He also won the British championship in Rotax junior and X30 Junior classes.

Daniel moved into single seaters with Argenti in the British F4 series and after a successful maiden season has been approached by multiple teams ahead of the 2023 season.

![Image 12: A 600x45 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/b636c8_3f29eabc449349caabf95bb640f2b3a1~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_600,h_45,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/b636c8_3f29eabc449349caabf95bb640f2b3a1~mv2.png)

![Image 13: NATHAN TYE-01.png](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/b636c8_fd91259c96f942dd949ff6c825c610f9~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_1060,h_534,al_c,q_90,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/NATHAN%20TYE-01.png)

![Image 14: NATHAN TYE-01.png](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/b636c8_1963929c55934f05b743f8455f2dc6f1~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_915,h_165,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/NATHAN%20TYE-01.png)

![Image 15: NTYEJUNIOR-02.png](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/b636c8_f4cc91de79df4aad86a27fc70c79b852~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_600,h_45,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/NTYEJUNIOR-02.png)

After winning the 2020 Ultimate karting championship, the series entered Nathan into the Iame I games held at Portimao in Portugal.

This was to be Nathan’s first international race and unknown to anyone at the time, the start of a very successful International career.

After finishing 3rd in the final, Nathan was spotted and picked up by the Sodi factory team.

Since then Nathan’s victory’s around the world securing the champions of the future title and 3rd in the FIA OKJ series has been defined as historic by many. Nathan Tye Jnr turned the spotlight not only on himself but also on the French team, long-awaited in the Junior and Senior classes.

Since the beginning of this year, Sodikart has been able to count on Tye to navigate in the front positions, happily so, thanks to results. Between WSK, COTF, and, above all, FIA Karting, Nathan has made sure that he can be present in the situations that count.

“In 2020 UKC was a new championship in the midst of Covid and we decided to sign up very last minute, literally days before it started. It was one of the best decisions we ever made and I went on to win the 2020 championship. Paul Phelan and the UKC team knew i was desperate to race in a European race, so my prize was an entry to the Iame I games. I made the podium on my 1st European race and was scouted by Sodikart, who offered me a trial in Italy. From this I was offered a full factory drive with their French team to compete on the OKJ category in the FIA champions of the future and WSK races. I will be eternally grateful for the opportunity UKC gave me."

Gabriel spent many years watching both his brothers compete in karting, travelling up and down the UK as well as across Europe, but didn’t himself sit in a kart until aged 10 years old.

His first club race was in 2018 at his local karting club Whilton Mill International Karting Circuit in Northamptonshire where he competed in just 11 Cadet Races before jumping straight into the IAME X30 Mini’s series in 2019 aged 12.

Since 2019 he has raced for the CROC-Promotions UK Karting Team, collecting his first notable title as CHAMPION at the PFI Mini X30 Winter Cup Series, and that’s when the dream started to become a reality, to race the best and climb the leaderboards in whatever class he competes in.

After winning the Ultimate karting championship in 2021, Gabriel has gone on to become double world champion in Junior X30, winning the title in both 2021 and 2022.

​Gabriel now races in Formula 4, competing throughout the UK and Europe.

![Image 19: Various go-karts zoom along the track, and a young man stands on a podium holding a trophy and a bottle of champagne](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/b636c8_d370482ed22d41d79d3bab751f8febb6~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_953,h_643,al_c,q_90,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/b636c8_d370482ed22d41d79d3bab751f8febb6~mv2.png)

![Image 20: lwatts-01.png](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/b636c8_ca2e8d59d9ab4b5a9414adfe6a88eed8~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_915,h_165,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/lwatts-01.png)

![Image 21: lwatts-02.png](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/b636c8_f7a5bb208a664d969a08a353c465d69c~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_600,h_45,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/lwatts-02.png)

After winning the 2020 series in the Junior category, Luke was provided with test day with Junior Ginetta champions R Racing.

After being immediately impressed with Luke’s driving, he was given a development program with the team that would see him take on a years testing before being provided with a race seat the following season.

Now part of the driver line up, Luke is enjoying a great deal if success and learning his craft in car racing, guided by the best in the business - R Racing.

![Image 22: Two side by side photographs, the left one shows a go-kart rider celebrating, the right one shows a team, a go-kart, and a big check with Ticket Rotax Max written on it](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/b636c8_9f921e2231d445b096e86f0293093d97~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_1281,h_547,al_c,q_90,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/b636c8_9f921e2231d445b096e86f0293093d97~mv2.png)

![Image 23: sbutcher-01.png](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/b636c8_496e0c0223b64e41bcc921ceb2fa5735~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_915,h_165,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/sbutcher-01.png)

![Image 24: sbutcher-02.png](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/b636c8_efc44f907dd94186bf038f570791cae9~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_600,h_45,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/sbutcher-02.png)

Sean took the title of the Senior Ultimate karting champion in 2021 with support from his team KR-SPORT.

Sean has since focused his efforts on the Rotax European championships and took 1st place in the standings to now be declared the 2022 Rotax European champion.
